hints: Focus on what an oxidising agent actually does, it gains electrons itself while it oxidises something else.
Count the electrons in each arrangement to identify the elements, look for who is one electron short of a full shell.
Compare the two non-metals from the same group and remember that the smaller atom at the top pulls in that extra electron most strongly.
walkthrough:
**Recall what makes a strong oxidising agent**

A strong oxidising agent is easily reduced. That means it really wants to gain electrons.

Think: non-metals near the top right of the Periodic Table, especially Group 17, are the best at this.

**Identify each element from its electrons**

Count total electrons to find proton number.

$$A: 1s^2 2s^2 2p^5 = 9 \text{ electrons = F, fluorine (2,7)}$$ $$B: 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 = 12 \text{ electrons = Mg, magnesium (2,8,2)}$$ $$C: 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^5 = 17 \text{ electrons = Cl, chlorine (2,8,7)}$$ $$D: 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 4s^2 = 20 \text{ electrons = Ca, calcium (2,8,8,2)}$$

**Pick the keenest electron-gainer**

B and D are Group 2 metals. They lose 2 electrons to form $2+$ ions, so they are reducing agents, not oxidising agents.

That leaves fluorine and chlorine, both Group 17 with 7 outer electrons needing just one more to get $ns^2np^6$. Fluorine is smaller, with less shielding and higher electronegativity, so it attracts that electron most powerfully and is the strongest oxidising agent.

options.A: Correct. This is fluorine, $1s^2 2s^2 2p^5$. With 7 outer electrons it needs only one more to complete its octet to $1s^2 2s^2 2p^6$. It is the most electronegative element, tiny with strong nuclear pull, so it gains electrons most readily and is the strongest oxidising agent here.
options.B: Incorrect. This is magnesium, $\text{Mg}$ with outer arrangement $3s^2$. Group 2 metals lose electrons to form $\text{Mg}^{2+}$. That makes magnesium a reducing agent (it is oxidised itself), the opposite of an oxidising agent.
options.C: Incorrect but tempting. This is chlorine, $\text{Cl}$ with outer arrangement $3s^2 3p^5$. Chlorine is a good oxidising agent, but it is larger than fluorine with an extra shell and more shielding, so its pull for an extra electron is weaker. Students who forget the trend down Group 17 often pick this.
options.D: Incorrect. This is calcium, $\text{Ca}$ with outer arrangement $4s^2$. Like magnesium, it is a Group 2 metal that loses electrons to form $\text{Ca}^{2+}$. It acts as a reducing agent, not an oxidising agent.
